findings.title: deleteCacheMutation never invalidates connectedCalendars, leaving stale cache status in the UI
findings.body: The deleteCache mutation's onSuccess only shows a toast and calls the optional onSuccess prop; unlike the disconnectMutation in the same file (which explicitly invalidates viewer.calendars.connectedCalendars and viewer.apps.integrations in onSettled), it does not invalidate the connectedCalendars query. After the user deletes the cache, the dropdown will still show the 'Cache Status / Last updated' entry and the 'Delete cached data' action until some parent happens to refetch, because cacheUpdatedAt comes from the connectedCalendars query data. Add utils.viewer.calendars.connectedCalendars.invalidate() (e.g. in onSettled) so the UI reflects the deletion.

findings.title: getCacheStatusByCredentialIds reports expired cache rows as valid cache status
findings.body: The groupBy query that powers the 'Cache Status' display does not filter on expiresAt, while the actual cache read path (getCachedAvailability) only serves rows with expiresAt >= now. A credential whose cache entries have all expired will still show 'Last updated: <timestamp>' and offer 'Delete cached data' in the UI, even though that data will never be served as a cache hit. The where clause should include expiresAt: { gte: new Date() } so the displayed status matches what the cache actually serves.

findings.title: ENV_FILE="../.env" is resolved relative to the caller's working directory, not the script location
findings.body: The script sets ENV_FILE="../.env", which is evaluated relative to wherever the developer runs the script from. Running the documented path from the repo root (./scripts/test-gcal-webhooks.sh) would create or modify a .env file in the directory above the repository instead of the repo's .env; conversely running it from inside scripts/ targets apps' parent incorrectly unless the layout matches exactly. It should resolve the path from the script's own directory, e.g. ENV_FILE="$(dirname "$0")/../.env".

findings.title: sed -i '' is macOS-only and fails on GNU sed (Linux)
findings.body: The script uses `sed -i '' -E ...`, which is the BSD/macOS syntax. On Linux (GNU sed), `-i ''` is interpreted as an in-place edit with the empty string treated as a filename argument, producing 'No such file or directory' and failing to update GOOGLE_WEBHOOK_URL. Since this script is committed for all developers, use a portable approach (e.g. `sed -i.bak -E ... file && rm file.bak`) or detect the platform.

findings.title: Access-denied case throws a plain Error instead of a TRPCError
findings.body: When the credential does not exist or belongs to another user, the handler throws `new Error("Credential not found or access denied")`. tRPC maps plain Errors to INTERNAL_SERVER_ERROR (HTTP 500) rather than a meaningful NOT_FOUND/FORBIDDEN code, so clients and monitoring see a server error for what is really a client/authz failure, and error-message handling on the client can't distinguish it from an actual crash. Throw `new TRPCError({ code: "NOT_FOUND" })` (or FORBIDDEN) instead.

findings.title: Cache timestamp is formatted with a hardcoded "en-US" locale, ignoring the user's locale
findings.body: The 'Last updated' timestamp is formatted with `new Intl.DateTimeFormat("en-US", ...)` regardless of the user's configured locale, so non-US users see US date/time conventions (e.g. MM/DD/YYYY) in an otherwise localized UI. Use the locale from useLocale()/i18n or pass undefined to Intl.DateTimeFormat so the browser/user locale is respected.

findings.title: No tests for the deleteCache mutation or the new repository status method
findings.body: This PR adds a mutation that deletes CalendarCache rows based on credential ownership, and a new getCacheStatusByCredentialIds repository method feeding the UI, but includes no tests. The ownership check (a user must not be able to delete cache for a credential they don't own, including negative in-memory delegation credential IDs) and the groupBy mapping are exactly the kind of logic that should be covered; the PR description's own checklist relies on manual end-to-end testing instead. At minimum, add a handler-level test covering success, wrong-owner, and nonexistent-credential cases.
